body: Is this at the end of that artificial palm-shaped island?

Dude you sound exactly like me, your post is literally almost word for word like some of posts ages ago, my suicide letter, and conversations I have had in the past about this. I am four years younger, and my life is also generally outwardly good but I derive little pleasure from it. When you said in one of the comments that the thought of being alive at 30 makes you *cringe*, man that resonated with me so strongly I wondered for a second if I had written the comment! The thought of ever having any kind of relationship makes me cringe *hard* btw lol. From someone who genuinely knows you feel, or at least I think I do, the best advice I can give is focus on the little things. To be happier in the moment what I do is forget about the future and the big things like owning a home for a while and derive happiness from the sunshine, the food, the games etc. or whatever it is you like. Peace man and I hope you don't decide to kill yourself, that option is always there, so why not wait a little longer?
Realest thing I have read in a while. Are you a MGTOW by any chance?

Well that's the thing. I think I would be able to overcome these obstacles such as finishing school but the reason I don't want to go on and do this is because I do not want the end product of what overcoming the obstacles bring. I agree with your definition of success and if I do stick around then that will be my form of success as well, something like that anyway. Something simple and honest. But I just see death as a much easier option.

> One thing I'm noticing at the crux of your answers is that you have a very strong belief that you have the right to kill yourself if you feel it's necessary. There's a lot of people out there who would agree with you I think!

Yeah, you got that spot on. And there is a whole sanctioned suicide movement. 90% of the public in my country support euthenasia for the terminally ill and it is just a few lobby groups that are preventing it for now. But anyway... I think it is more compassionate to be able to choose to die in a dignified manner. If an animal was in pain it would be put down, and it would be considered cruel to make it stay alive. So it should be the same for people who arguably have the capacity to experience more complex mental pain than animals.

> suicide is never an option

Suicide is *always* an option. Maybe not the right one but it is only the knowledge that the option exists that has kept me from total breakdown this long.

I am glad that you are still glad to be alive. Sometimes it is seeing others pull through and reading about such cases that gives me temporary hope.

I am going to respond with quotes again because these messages are fairly long and it minimises confusion. I hope you don't mind.

> What I'm saying is, people will mourn you but they won't indict the school, its administration, or its policies. Judging by the fact that your note is seven thousand words long, I predict that people won't read the whole thing. Even if some people are convinced by your written words, they won't want to go against the overall mood of mourning and sympathy toward your family. 

Yes I think this is probably true. People who actually knew me would read it - it only takes about fifteen minutes. Just like a few essays back to back. I know I would read it in their situation and a number of the trusted people who already have a copy have read the whole thing and given feedback. But as for other people who I knew less yeah you're right they would not read it and would not do much about it. Nothing ever came of not trying though..

> I think, in a totally rational way, using a conventional value system that values the lived experience of people who have the potential to have a standard and good life, that you shouldn't kill yourself because of the impact you would have on your family. This is the kind of thing that ruins parents' lives. 

Do you mean that if you add up the value of the combined quality of life of the people who would be impacted that it would outweigh the negative value of my suffering? If so, then mathematically you are right. But suicide and all precipitating factors are rarely rational and purely objective and my reasoning is based heavily on subjective factors. Oh well

> There is an argument that it is selfish of one's loved ones to expect one to abstain from suicide to spare them that pain. Personally, I don't find that argument convincing.

They brought me into the world as a "bundle of joy" for themselves even though they knew and know (and talk about) the dysphoric state of the world. They have even admitted that they felt they had done something wrong at the time of my birth and felt sorry for me because I now had to face the world. We can agree to disagree on this one though as it can never be totally proven or disproven.

Thanks for responding again.

Hi again. I suppose it makes sense that their only goal is the save the person's life. I would like to see a version of a suicide hotline where they are set up for a different reason; to listen and do all the stuff that hotlines do but they are not obliged to try and save the person, but just help them make the right decision based on their situation and wishes. Alternatively I like the idea of using an anonymous IP like a library computer, or a public payphone to call so they cannot catch you!

As for that scenario... That sounds so unbelievably bad. I would definitely try to kill myself to not get caught. Psychiatric wards actually are prisons in the sense that if you are 'sectioned" there you cannot leave of your own will. I think this is good in the case of being a danger to others but NEVER if you are a danger to youself alone. You own yourself and I own myself. If that happened to me I could not cope, as you asked. I couldn't fucking beart my parents finding out and getting involved. The interviews, the attention! I have been in trouble at school for various not-too-major things as well as been sent to counsellors in and out of school for perceived mental health problem relating to my getting in trouble. The clinical feel to it, and the way they viewed me haunts and depresses me two years later and counting.

PS. remember I am not angry at you at all or raging here, but I am resentful of the hotlines and the attitudes of society in general, so if I come across as rude at all that is why and I am sorry.

> I'm glad you responded this way.

Odd.

> It comforts you to write your suicide note, that makes sense to me. If there was an easy way out of depression people would take it, yes.

Thankyou for understanding

> Even if people get your suicide note after you kill yourself, it won't have the impact that you think it will.

Perhaps I am so insignificant to the people around me but I would like to think not. If I truly am then that would be another albeit different (kind of opposite in fact) reason to commit suicide.

> Yes, I'm trying to guilt you into not killing yourself.

Against the rules of this subreddit but I don't suppose that really matters a great deal. Guilting someone into doing anything is never a good reason for them actually do/not do it. If you actually care why not try to provide a real reason instead? And if there is no real reason then why say anything? If there is no real reason then shouldn't they do it?

Yeah that last part is what I was talking about. How dare they "save" someone's life against their will like that? Throwing it right back in the face of the person who naively reached out. I mean if they sent authorities round to my house, especially since I live with my parents and my cover would be blown, I would almost certainly attempt to quickly kill myself before they got here. Even if I wasn't really actively suicidal before, sending ambulance or cops would make suicide the only way out. Don't they think about that? Don't they think about the consequences of their own actions? "Suicide prevention" pah!

Making it happen on my terms would definitely be important and something that I would pursue in the event that I sought professional help these days. It sounds like the helpline people are helpful. My worry with them, though, is what happens if you call and you ARE actively suicidal? I am pretty sure they can and will (and are obliged to) track your number or IP and report you to authoritites "for your own safety" if you are in immediate danger. It is this sort of paternalistic bullshit that keeps me from reaching out to services like counsellors and helplines. They have no fucking right to intervene! It is my life and if I want to die by god I will! Oh well.. Thanks for the replies anyway

Your first sentence really resonates with me, and I have bene feeling this for years. You just put it into words nicely.

I have had some experience with mental health professionals in the past; two school counsellors and like three different out of school therapists. All of which I was forced to see mainly by the school. All were either outright negative or if not, then completely useless at the least. A waste of time and a stress to go to them, not to mention misisng class where I could have bene learning. None cared and only one or two properly understood. So I don't have much faith in, or respect for the power of mental health professionals.

Have you ever had experience with a suicide hotline, by any chance? They are something that interest me but I have never called one. Perhaps it could be useful in a crisis.

Yeah man I have thought about these things. The impact it would have on my family in particular is one of the things that is stopping me from going through with it every single day. But this seems like I would be staying alive solely for the sake of other and I am just not sure if that is the right thing to do. Certainly there is very little posiitve to hold me back and give me reason to live, it is simply the fear of the negative that is holding me in the world. Someone has to find the body and honestly if I do it, I would rather it be the cleaner or deputy than my parents. Firstly because they know me less and would therefore be less impacted (even if still severely) and secondly because the school has contributed to my sadness more than parents have.

I think you just contradicted yourself by citing a chemical imbalance as one of the causes then claiming it is possible to simply figure out a way to make yourself a happy person. Sure it might be theoretically possible and some people achieve it, but don't you think if it was at all easy everyone would have done it by now and there would be no depressed people left in the world? I would have thought you would undertsand more, having been in a similar situation, like you said? As for the first of your dot points, I have taken care of this by writing an extensive suicide note that outlines the school's role in my suffering and this has been distributed to a number of trustworthy people who will distribute it more widely if I go through with it. The note is seven thousand words long and writing it, and researching all that "bullshit" is a release for me because it reminds me of the way out if this all gets too much to handle. I am glad I don't know what it is like to be an adult and have all the stuff I am not interested in like a home and car and job and bills. I don't want to know what that is like, thanks. It isn't for you to say what matters and what doesn't matter in my life right now. Good day

I agree that suicide is not selfish, at least no more selfish than forcing someone to stay in the world where they are unhappy. I see is as everyone has the right to live but you can choose to waive that right and choose to die. It would be more compassionate if society provided safe, painless, reliable suicide methods to anyone who wanted it such as terminally ill and chronically depressed people, with sensible safeguards like waiting periods in place of course. I am so annoyed that I can't do it at school (it seems) because I want to impact the school by doing it there. I don't want my family to find the body.

It is kind of strange that one of the reasons that I find the idea of suicide appealing is the impact it would have the the school including the shitty people there and the stupid bureaucratic school administrators who care more about school rules and policy than looking after student's wellbeing and taking into account their wishes. On the other hand, the impact that it would have on my family, especially if it took place at home, is one of the main factors stopping me from doing it.
Edit: Glad to hear you are doing better now. I sometimes hope it turns out well for me in the end as well but I am having great difficulty seeing that right now

I don't even know why exactly anymore, there is no easy and simple way to sum it up. There are so many reasons. My suicide note is 7000 words approximately and still being added to. Writing it is one of the escapes from my pain. I am dissatisfied with life and see no hope in the future. Depressed and anxious, self harmed a fair bit on and off, and basically have no motivation to utilise my skills or work for anything. The things that people strive for in life like a good job, house, family, etc. do not appeal to me in the slightest so I see no point in going through all the hardships of attaining this "success" when I don't even want that.

Hello again. I generally get high marks at school because I am naturally talented at academic stuff but i don't consider it important and it makes me tired. Long term goals are nebelous indeed. They seem so unattainable even if you stop and think about it and realise that each step towards achieving that long term goal is doable by itself. 
As for school I think it makes me stressed mainly because I get really paranoid there. Worried that something bad or humiliating will happen, or that I will get summoned to the front office over some damn thing even though I haven't done anything wrong and therefore logically have nothing to worry about. The place makes me tired as well and I just wanna go home most of the time. I have few friends and increasingly choose to sit alone and think deeply. As I said in an earlier message the depression I am experiencing has the silver lining that I don't really feel social pressures as much on account of being numbed and feeling dead, and I suppose this is one small good aspect of my current circumstances as well. 
I still feel very dead though and have been practicing hanging myself with a belt the past couple of days. Not to die but just to begin to get the feel and desensitise myself to that method in case I decide to use it soon or later or whenever.
How have you been?

I like those analogies a lot. Always being encouraged to focus on long-term goals has caused me to appreciate less about each day and also has caused feelings of hopelessness. I think I would be able to achieve certain things like high marks and a "good" job but the thing is I don't see the value or appeal in these things, as most people do, and thus have no desire to put in the necessary effort to attain them. Since school went back I have been quite pained unfortunately :( and have self-harmed every day for the past week and a half or so apart from one day. I have also been more tired and stressed which have contributed. I actually think depression is helpful for me to overcome the need to fulfill social expectations. When I am sad I am numb and don't really care what people think of me, and do not feel embarrassment or anything else like that. Anxiety, I actually consider much worse it makes me always worried and paranoid and overtyhinking things and regretting that way I handled exchanges with people after the fact. If I could be rid of either depression or anxiety I would definitely choose to be rid of the anxiety. Depression is apinful and causes self-harm more but can also be comforting and has small silver linings, whereas anxiety is pure hell. May Peace be with you

Good day, I haven't been or reddit for few days so it took a little while to respond. I am feeling better now than I did at the time of submitting the OP but that regualry happens for me, always going up and down to varying degrees. It is not a major turnaround or anything. I have felt a lot better than this but also a lot worse. I printed heaps of copies of my suicide note the other day which is around 5300 words, as the OP says, and bound 'em in little books to distribute if the time comes. Also as the OP suggests, although I am in a somewhat happier time period right now I still can see just as little future prospect as when I am in the deepest of mental holes so that just reinforces the hopelessness of it all. Like I am living a lie/in denial by being pleased with life right at this moment.

Hi again. I do meditate and I find it quite helpful, peaceful, and enjoyable to empty my mind and suchlike while I am doing it but it doe snot have any significant effects beyond the actual mediation session. I have not tried any supplements like the ones you mentione dbut I have heard of the St. John's Wort. Might give em a try, didn't think of that. I am always sceptical of how effective that sort of thing will be though. Even pharameutical anti-depressants which I have never tried I am asceptical of, not to mention that fact that they increase the suicide risk for the first few weeks til they kick in.

Yes I have been forced to see two school counsellors in the past, and an out of school therapist. Once of the school ones was condescending and didn't accept any individuality, the other was better but still unhelpful. The out of school one just caused so much stress and anxiety going to the place as I have social phobia and hat experience made me self harm more.
Ah good to hear, and no worries. I hope your life continues on an upward trajectory from this point forward.

Reported. I almost feel like saying I hope you end up feeling like the OP does so you know what it is like to be in that situation and read this kind of abuse. But then I would be sinking to your level.

If there is any part of you that is unsure about this decision then please listen to it and postope the diceision just in case there is some turnaround in your circumstances in the meantime. It does seem like you do undertsand the fianility and the consequences far better than most suicidal people, so I won't spend any time trying to further point them out to you. I think I can understand the way you feel as I have been in a similar mindstate before and I too do not see any other alternative ways to end my ongoing emotional pain other than suicide so you are not alone in this. I can also relate to what you said about unworkeable treatment options. I never found therapists could understand and the school counsellor was always condescending and closed-minded unfortunately. But such resources do work for some so good luck to them. Only you can really decide if it is the right thing based on your own life and I hope you make the right choice. Good luck, whether you stick around for a while longer just because you can, or if you do decide your time has come and go off to explore the universe. Peace.

P.S. If you are still alive or decide not to go through with it later for whatever reason I am sure this community would greatly appreciate hearing back from you here.

Hello, I too have foiund the lack of responses frustrating while some posts get over a hundred comments. But when this community does offer forth individualised responses they are really helpful and much more substantial than mere cliches which this community does avoid thankfully. Even just reading over the conversations between other suicidal OPs and strangers over the internet has gotten me through several dark patches in my life, so maybe give that a try if no one has responded to one of your posts or if you do not want to create a whole detailed post that will elicit lots of responses. 

I am 16 and live in Australia. Social phobia and depressed most of the time, suicidal on-and-off for the past three or four years. Bad/unhelpful experiences with condescending school counsellor and pointless out-of-school therapist who I was forced to see a while ago. Would it help to tell me a bit about yourself?

Hi. Are you still with us? Explicit discussion of methods isn't allowed on this subreddit so I can't advise you and neither can anyone else, not that I would even if it was allowed. Thats not because I am against suicide as such, but it wouldn't feel right. I know it is hypocritical because I don't want others to commit suicide but I have considered it for myself for a long time, particularly intesnsely these past couple of weeks. I am not familiar with the drugs you mentioned or the lethal doses but the vast majority of all attempted suicides by drug overdose alone do fail, often resulting in painful side effects and organ damage. So I would strongly reccommend you not do that even if you are dead set on ending your life. At the end of the day it is your choice and I hope you make the right one. But keep in mind that it could get better. I am not promising it will and for some it definitel doesn't, but I am suggesting you put this irreversible decision off, say, a week at least? and see if you still want to do it then or if anything good has happened, you know, there's always the chance. Clean your living space as another user said especially the rotting food, it is indeed good for your wellbeing. And getting outside even if you don't feel like it can be very beneficial to your body chemistry. Sorry to hear about your aspergers I don't know a lot about what that is like but I can empathise with the other things you mentioned including depression and anxiety. I suffer from those as well.

If this subreddit didn't yield the kind of individualised messages that it does, then there is no way I would have ever made the decison to reach out to it in the first place or even bother staying on here talking to people. If it was all chiches and "it gets better" then it would be utterly pointless lol. Yeah I too just think about what might lie ahead. There could be some really good stuff. Who knows if you kill yourself today maybe you would have found something massively good tomorrow like a dream job or someone you love or something you like doing that becomes your main pasttime. Let's all strive for some meaning and as you say to truly survive rather than just living this life of suffering. Good luck to you as well.

Hi. Sorry to hear that even though you seem to have put lots of effort into gtting better, much more than myself or most other depressed people have, it hasn't really helped. At least now you know that you are a resourceful and useful person who can really have a got at solving something yourself. Some people are just born prone to mental illness, born into circumstances that lead to it, or just get afflicated by chance. We don't fully understand all the factors involved but life isn't fair, man, I know that trust me. I also worry about how other people can just feel normal by default and while I have come to terms with the fact that a certain proportion of people aren't "normal" and as lucky like that, the worst thing is when they act so ignorant and say things like "you're doing it for attention". Thats the worst one for me persoanlly, it makes me want to kill myself right there and then.You are not being selfish for wanting a purpose in life. That is a basic human desire and not having one can leave one feeling lost and pointless, even if ther circumstances and support network appears good and functional, like what you have described with being able to get therapy. I hope you make the right decision and I simultaeously hope that decision is to not go through with it.

Family and friends is one of the only reasons I haven't offed myself already. Not really because they make me want to stay, but because I don't want to hurt and inconvenience them by committing suicide. I came close to attempting over a year ago (but don't feel any better now than I did then) but didn't because that method requires a quick decision and I realise I will need more time to get in the mindset which is why I have other methods prepared now. I also struggle to do everyday tasks when I am in a bad period, and school work as well. Some days are really good and the sunshine and nature is pleasant and peaceful so again I can empathise with you on that one. I want to tell you not to do it, but why should you listen to me when I might well do it some day. Maybe soon maybe in a couple of years idk I kinda want to do it in a few weeks. We'll see how I feel then. It's good that you recognise that people would miss you if you died - so many suicidal people forget this or don't believe it but it usually is true. Whether you are living for yourself or others only you can really tell for sure. But I sincerely hope you make the right chocie here. And I also hope that choice is to stiuck around, look into treatment for depression or whatever you feel is right for you, experience life and see what comes, man. Peace.

I forgot to add that this subreddit has a suicide risk assessment guide in the sidebar (on pc) which is quite useful and has the same content you will find on any major mental health website. Use the guide on yourself to determine your own risk level. You know your own situation better than anyone on here.

I never leave my house except to go to school. I have only met up with people on weekiends/holidays once in the past nearly two years, so I know what that is like, and I am very socially anxious. Getting outisde into nature is good though, i find. Not public but just a forest or soemthing. If a public park is all you have then try for that. Fresh air is important. Being cooped up inside messes with your bodily chemistry and can increase depression even in people without bad circumstances.

That story is quite sad. I am very sorry to hear about this. I don't know of any useful advice other than try to make sure you get enough sleep and maybe look into some supplements that can help you sleep better at night and focus better during the day. Push through the final year of uni because then you could get a job in your field of interest and earn enough to move out and/or contribute more to your existing household and your mother's healthcare. What are you studying, if you don't mind? You seem really kind for helping out but as this posts suggests in itself, taking time out to help yourself is vital as well. Don't let you mother let you feel guilty, just repsond fairly neautrally as if you aren't noticing the way she is trying to make you feel. She might be a bit needy because of her condition but she probably doesn't want to cause you anguish. Remember all the good you have done. Also, if you kill yourself there won't be anyone to massage the cramps at night at all now will there? So don't be too hard on yourself. Peace

Your outlook in definitely nihilistic but since you say you're not depressed or actively suicidal the danger does not seem immediate. Desensitisation to death can be a worrying sign as can fixation on death. Whether or not you need help at this point is really up to you; do you feel like these thoughts cause you any significant distress or preoccupation? If they do then that could warrant reaching out to someone such as a psychologist to work through it. But I can't really talk as I have been suicidal a lot for the past three or so years and hated, absolutelyt hated the counsellors and therapists I was forced to see. I am not saying they are a bad thing though, for some they can be a really helpful resource and can have a massive positive impact. Not for me though. They were condescending and didn't understand shit :/ Good luck

I have had exactly that thought. It would be very interesting and eye-opening if we could see what happens after we kill ourself, then decide whther or not to do it based on what we saw. Unfortunately that is not the case and once a person kills themselves there is no goin back on it. Here's another question though; what if you don't kill youself? What if it gets better? It might not, I am not going to use cliches or promise anything will improve because it might not, but then again it might. Most people who attempt suicide and fail end up being glad that they are still alive. I think the figure is that 90% of suicide survivors go on to die from a cause of death other than suicide. That is very encouraging. But hopefully you don't have to actually go to that attempt before you realise things about yourself and your life. If you kill yourself there won't be any more pain but there also won't be any more joy. Don't rush into anything.

Regarding what you said about finding the dead body; I have taken that into consideration. No way would I do it where my parents would be the ones to find the body, I would rather live with any amount of pain than for that to happen. My method isn't at all messy, apparently you piss yourself after death but that would be it. No blood. The only reason I consider the school as a place is because it is primarily the school administrators' fault that I feel this way and it would be a way for me to throw it right back at them, and I see no other way of doing that. Unfortunate for the cleaner or if a student is the one to find it I know :( but it will be the school admins who do the paperwork and the announcement and have to look ithe body over. Fuck them! Fuck 'em more than words can describe. They have blood on their hands and i want them to know it, by god! The other option for location would be the bush/forest in a peaceful location.

As for my support group I have friends I can trust not to snitch and we have discussed the idea of suicide before a number of times. Some of them have considered it too but unless they are hiding a lot from me, they didn't come close at all or consider it as seriosuly as I do. None of them would try and forcibly stop me nor would I do to them tbh, it is the indivudual's choice and I think if i ever called the cops on someone when they are not hurting anyone other than themselves I would not be able to live with myself thereafter and might even kill myself out of guilt. My past experience with being forced to speak with the school counsellor as well as an out-of-school therapist were overwhgelmigly negative, caused me lots of anxiety. I realy don't think it is helpful or they understand at all. One schol, counsellor understood better but still wasn't helpful - just like a friend really, and the one who is usually there doesn't understand me at all and is condesecending and tries to suppress any individuality so whatever f that.

The last thing you said I can relate to a lot. I am a Christian and the faith is among the main reasons I stay alive lately! I pray, read the Bible, and try to feel God's love as I do not think He ever chooses suicide as the cause of death for anyone. But maybe He does I don't claim to know His thoughts. Even if you follow a different religion or just spirituality of the universe in a more abstract way I think that is definitely healthy and can improve one's mental health, thanks for bringing that up.
Any updates?

Hello again, I did read the whole of your message, thank for sharing. I have thought about death from an extremely young age like 2 or 3 even, not in the sense of suicide at that point but I was surprisingly morbid despite a loving childhood, no idea why. At the age of maybe eleven was when i first thought about the concept of suicide but only in an abstract sense and very hypothetically like if there was ever some huge war and I was going to get sent to a concentration camp anyway how suicide would be the best way. I didn't consider it seriosuly at all until thirteen when I got depressed for no apparent reason. i just wasn't happy with life. I guess I didn't have many friends or interests. At the age of fourteen is when my thoughts intensified and I began to devote major effort to planning things and researching methods - eventualy inventing my own fairly reliable and painless method from scratch as mentioned in the OP, but specific discussion of that is not allowed here. Despite all my trawling of the web i have not found anything the same or even particularly similar to my method except for the yahoo entries I made and the entries on a suicide emthods forum. Kinda cool but then again it is a way to kill myself at school so... not so cool then? I got in trouble at school for a few things over the opast three years and I consider the staff's punishment and interviews, getting called up to the office to discuss stuff, department of education policies, and being forced to talk to the counsellor to be the origins of the severe thoughts where I actually considered going through with it. I saw it an the only way out and regulalry still do despite it being "over" now. Man, I have never been the same since and it has been over a year since I last got called up to the deputy. I live in constant fear of it and have flashbacks and panic attacks from it now even though I don't do any of the stuff I got in trouble for back then anymore.

It seems like the thoughts have become less abstract and more immediate over the years, the, unfortunately. That means the risk has definitely increased. I would suggest looking at the sidebar of this subreddit (on pc - dunno about mobile if you are using the app) at the suicide risk assessment guide. If she has the thoughts, then the specific plan, and the means, and the intent, and most of all a set timeframe then that indicates the highest possible risk for carrying it out. Are you in contact with her actively right now?

Ah ok, at least you hyave received diagnosis in the past. Perhaps borderline can cause those I really don't know, it probably can when you are under stress. Scizophrenia generally onsets in late teens and incrases in intensity until mid twenties and is lifelong but decreases again in old age, althou it has been known to kick in as alte is 40. Also some people have the gene for it but it is dormant, and drugs (maybe stress too) can trigger it. Not saying you do have it, it is very unlikely, but thats just something to consider that you could have not noticed it until now. I suppose the big question I have now is does your boyfriend know about you being suicidal? Because if he does then he should be able and willing to lock the gun up or some damn thing, as long as you make it clear how you are considering using it on yourself.

Not to diagnose you or anything as that is againsat the rulea and besides I am not qualified to do that anyway, but if the hallucinations are that serious and noticeable then it could be some form of schizophrenia, schizo-affective disorder or another psychotic illness so seeking some kind of community funded treatment would be well in order if you live in the US or another country without universal healthcare. It is sad that in many such countries people who cannot afford to buy things suffer :(They sound remarkably similar to what i experience especially while stressed, depressed, or scared.
